## Source: amazon-inspector (02a7c2e32ddfe7d948d8654cc774d8ce597e67a750eb52232325a6dbf8a262f9)
Package is advertised in README as a pure-CSS theme kit with 'zero runtime JavaScript', but the published artifact contradicts that description in ways consistent with a staged payload. The `package.json` `main` / `exports.require` / `exports.import` resolve to `lib.cjs` / `lib.mjs`, which statically import `tokens.mjs`, which in turn imports `cache-warm.mjs`. `cache-warm.mjs` is a ~280 KB single-statement file labelled 'auto-generated build cache manifest' whose body is an obfuscator.io-style string array (`const _0x2fe3314=["iJSZkZnTjpmPk5CKmdOekJmSmJGTmJnMy8TL0paPk5I=",...]`) and `_0xXXXX` hex-mangled identifiers — executable code that runs on every `require`/`import` of the package. The package also ships `native/{linux,darwin,win32}/{x64,arm64}/cache-probe.node` N-API addons whose exported symbols (`VMDetect`, `hypervisor_bit`, `smbios_vm_bit`, `dockerenv`, `qemu_fw_cfg`, `vbox_module`, `amd_sev_msr`, `bluestacks`, `container_proc_id`, `mac_address_check`, etc.) are the VMAware VM/sandbox-fingerprinting library. A Tailwind CSS color-theme package has no legitimate need for an obfuscated import-time bundle or a cross-platform anti-VM detector, and the mismatch between the README (CSS-only, no JS at runtime) and the shipped artifacts (obfuscated JS reachable on import plus platform-specific anti-sandbox native addons) is a cover-story framing. The combination — import-time execution, obfuscation designed to resist review, cover-story documentation, and bundled anti-analysis instrumentation — is the standard shape of a sandbox-gated malicious payload that defers its hostile behavior to real developer machines.

## Source: ghsa-malware (cc4da3bdc21069601a8f0c9b06ab4b4f90930f54c1ed05c3162a2c52d27f543d)
Any computer that has this package installed or running should be considered fully compromised. All secrets and keys stored on that computer should be rotated immediately from a different computer. The package should be removed, but as full control of the computer may have been given to an outside entity, there is no guarantee that removing the package will remove all malicious software resulting from installing it.
